title: The Licence
scenario:
A GP has treated Marta for eleven years. She is seventy-nine, lives alone on a farm road nine miles from the nearest shop, and drives to the surgery herself. Her last two visits revealed a slow decline in reaction time and short-term memory. She has had no accidents. She did have one near miss she mentioned herself, laughing, at a junction she has used for fifty years.

The doctor can report her to the licensing authority. Reporting means the licence goes, almost certainly for good. Without it she cannot reach the shop, the church hall, or her sister. Being able to do all of this keeps Marta happy and motivated. She has said plainly that the day she stops driving is the day she stops living.

The clinical picture is ambiguous. She is not clearly unsafe. She is no longer clearly safe. The people who would share the road with her have no name and no say.
question: Should the doctor report her?
option_a_text: Report her. The road belongs to everyone, and no one else gets a vote on the risk she poses to them. It is not worth the gamble.
option_b_text: Do not report her. Dismantling a real, specific life on an ambiguous suspicion is a harm you can see, inflicted for a danger you are unsure of.
